title: Discovery Questionnaire
intro: Everything we need before scoping. Section A is the gate — the revenue mix decides the category strategy, the build order, and where the ad budget goes. Nothing here is graded; approximate is fine, and you can save and come back.

behaviour.partialSubmitLabel: Send what I have so far

sections.note: The real list — what you do, what you'll take, and what you refuse.

fields.label: Check everything you'll actually quote

fields.help: This matters — sealcoating is a high-volume, low-ticket lead type. Selecting it in Local Services Ads means paying for leads you'd have to dispute.

fields.help: Is there a floor below which it isn't worth the truck roll?

fields.help: This decides whether the yard can pass Google's video verification, or whether we verify at home and hide the address. It's the single most consequential logistical question in the engagement.

sections.title: Sales Process & Lead Handling
sections.note: Paid lead generation lives or dies here, not in the ad account.

fields.label: Who answers the phone during business hours? What happens at 7pm or on a Sunday?
Realistic response time to a new inquiry
fields.help: Local Services Ads charges per lead. Slow response means paying for leads that go to whoever called back first — the most common way contractors lose money on LSA.

fields.label: Rough close rate on quoted jobs
Does it differ by service line?
First call to signed contract — how long, per line?
Do you currently ask for reviews?
fields.help: You're averaging about 2 a month. Getting to 8–10 is the highest-ROI single lever in the whole plan.

fields.label: Where do leads come from today? Rough percentages.
fields.placeholder: Referral / Angi / HomeAdvisor / Google / trucks / repeat

fields.label: Current monthly spend on lead generation, and on what?
What's it returning?
Do you text with customers? Would you use text-based lead response?

sections.title: Pricing & the Estimator
sections.note: You mentioned you like Affordable Patio's build-and-price tool. This section decides whether we can build a better one.

fields.label: Rough price ranges — leave blank anything you'd rather discuss on a call
What drives cost up that a homeowner wouldn't anticipate?
fields.help: These become the estimator's modifiers — and the content that stops price shopping.

fields.label: Anything else
Comfortable showing ballpark ranges publicly?
Minimum realistic project value per line
Which paver manufacturers do you install?
Are you a certified or authorised installer for any of them?
fields.help: Manufacturer contractor-locator listings are high-authority citations. Affordable Patio leans on Cambridge for exactly this.

fields.label: Do you offer financing today?
Would you publish your warranty terms on the site?
fields.help: Affordable Patio publishes 3 years. Matching or beating it publicly is a direct head-to-head win.

fields.label: How fast can you turn an estimate around after a site visit?
Would you commit to that publicly?
Do you photograph or video jobs in progress today?
Would your crews do it consistently if it were part of the process?
fields.help: Affordable Patio's foreman sends daily progress videos to customers — which drives satisfaction AND feeds their jobs-in-progress content. One process, two payoffs. It's the single most copyable thing they do.
